en: Therīgāthā 2.2 Jentā Therīgāthā I have crossed over the flood; I am now free from debt. I have reached the further shore; I am now without fear. Having abandoned all attachments, I dwell in peace. I am a nun who has attained liberation. I was born into a wealthy family, endowed with great fortune. My father was a merchant, and my mother was likewise. I was the eldest daughter, possessed of beauty and grace. Then, seeing the Buddha, the Great Sage, the One with Vision, I went forth into homelessness, seeking the state of peace. Having seen the Teacher, I took refuge in him. I am now one who has cut off the stream of existence; I have transcended birth and death, and am no longer subject to them. With the destruction of the taints, I have realized for myself the state of Arhatship, cool and peaceful. I have attained the goal; I have lived the holy life. There is nothing further to be done; I am free from all bonds. I have reached the end of suffering; I am now at peace. I am a nun who has attained liberation.
all of them have been developed by me.”
Just as it was taught by the Buddha:
"For I have seen that Blessed One;
this is my final physical aggregation."
"The wandering on in birth is exhausted;
now there is no further becoming.
Thus indeed did the elder nun Jentā speak these verses.
